chapters.title: Abstract
chapters.html:
This work sets out an integral model of perception organized around nine basic fields. By a field we mean neither a physical region nor an organ, but a stable mode in which reality unfolds for an observer and, at the same time, the manner of its perception is set. It is shown that the nine fields form an ordered system in which each field possesses its own phenomenology, a characteristic type of energetic dynamics, and three positions of manifestation. The vertical organization of the fields, the mechanics of time and an applied aspect — bodily encoding — are treated separately. The proposed systematization is descriptive in character and rests on an internally consistent conceptual apparatus.

Keywords: perception, field, potential and manifestation, phenomenology of consciousness, energetic dynamics, time.

chapters.title: 1. Introduction
chapters.html:
The problem of describing perception is traditionally complicated by the fact that the observer is not separated from the observed: the way consciousness organizes experience enters into the composition of the experience itself. The present essay proceeds from the assumption that such organization is not arbitrary but is subject to a limited number of stable modes. These modes we call fields.

Nine fields in all are distinguished. Their sequence is not accidental: it reproduces the movement from the utmost shaped, structural mode of experience to the integral mode, in which the remaining fields appear as particular facets. Between these poles lie the fields of space, time, transformation, center, movement, communication and boundary. Such a sequence allows the model to be regarded at once as a classification and as a description of a process.

The first four fields describe the inner arrangement of experience — the way in which form arises out of unmanifested potential and how it is drawn into temporal dynamics. The subsequent fields (from the fifth to the eighth) describe experience from the side of the object: the point of concentration of attention, movement itself, the manifold of shaped paths, and the boundary of perception. The ninth field occupies a special position, since it thematizes not a single aspect but the integrity of the system as such.

chapters.title: 2. Three Positions of Manifestation
chapters.html:
Each field may be in one of three positions, and the position determines the mode of its action. Let us designate the first position MA. It corresponds to potential: the content is already given in a folded form but is not yet present in space — like a seed in which a future structure is compressed. Let us designate the second position ZHI; to it corresponds manifestation: the content is unfolded and given as a present form. The intermediate position KUN should be understood not as a simple midpoint but as a transition — the moment in which the folded begins to unfold. It is here that the resulting effect of the meeting of potential and action arises.

A convenient illustration is the development of an organism out of the genetic code: the inbuilt program is manifested successively in time, and the observed form is the result of its unfolding. In this sense any perceived phenomenon travels one and the same path — from folded potential, through transition, to shaped manifestation.

The positions are also significant for describing dysfunctions. A distortion in the position of potential is passive in character: energy finds no outlet, closes upon itself and leads to stagnation. A distortion in the position of manifestation, on the contrary, is active: energy is realized excessively, in hypertrophied fashion, and is directed outward in a destructive manner. A disturbance in the position of transition means the loss of the link between design and its embodiment, in consequence of which effort proves fruitless.

chapters.title: 3.1. Logos — the Field of Structure
chapters.html:
Content of the field. The first field posits reality as structure. Its content is systematicity in the pure state: hierarchy, causal connection, the geometry of relations, the foundation on which the rest is held. The metaphor of a skeleton is apt — a load-bearing structure that determines form yet is itself immobile.

Phenomenology. In phenomenological terms Logos is a code unfolding from potential into form. Its logic is not derived from anything else and in this sense is primary. In the position of potential the code is utterly compressed and, outside space, unmanifested; in the position of manifestation it is unfolded and given as a present object. The transition between them is an act of unfolding, analogous to the realization of an inbuilt program.

Energetic dynamics. The energetic dynamics of the field is described as a descending movement through hierarchical levels: each subsequent level rests on the previous, the flow is strict and admits no deviation. Bodily, the field is correlated with the lower supports — the legs and feet, where the movement closes and grounds itself.

Positions of manifestation. In the position of potential an inner knowledge of rules and systemic relations predominates; in the position of manifestation, the capacity to establish order, discipline and workable structures; in the position of transition, stability and reproducibility of the result are attained.

Resource expression. With a free flow of energy the field manifests as an inclination to order the disparate, to seek out the load-bearing principles of a situation, to think in categories of cause and effect and to translate designs into concrete plans.

Distortions. Passive distortion is expressed in ossification: structure ceases to be living, rules are observed for their own sake. Active distortion takes the form of imposing one's own order, in which hierarchy becomes an instrument of suppression. A disturbance of transition gives rise to a dead structure — a mechanism running idle.

Conditions of decline. The field loses force in environments of total chaos, under the demand for pure spontaneity, and where systematicity is identified with bureaucracy.

chapters.title: 3.2. Nima — the Field of Space
chapters.html:
Content of the field. The second field discloses reality as space that contains emptiness. Past, present and future coexist within it in a single moment; this is the field of possibilities and vectors through which a change of reality is admissible.

Phenomenology. It is essential that space here contains no inner architecture and is subject to no laws: it is prior to all form. There is no process of expansion within it — only boundlessness as such is present. The boundaries usually ascribed to space belong to the perceiving mind and can therefore be pushed back. Space is not a substance; it is able to contain any architecture, and the room for it is inexhaustible. Manifestation arises only when structure enters this space.

Energetic dynamics. Energy issues from the center evenly in all directions, like diverging rays, and gathers back to the center with the same ease. The movement is even, devoid of tension. Bodily, the field is correlated with the region of the pelvis.

Positions of manifestation. In the position of potential the holding of a multitude of possibilities predominates; in the position of manifestation, the ability to see connections and contexts; in the position of transition reality acquires volume and new paths open.

Resource expression. The resource manifestation is the simultaneous holding of several scenarios, calm amid uncertainty, the ability to change the state of affairs by a simple expansion of context, and freedom to move beyond the habitual.

Distortions. Passive distortion turns into an emptiness in which an abundance of possibilities paralyzes choice. Active distortion manifests as chaos in which all support is lost. A disturbance of transition leaves boundlessness without a point of application of forces.

Conditions of decline. The field declines in rigidly dogmatic systems, under closed conditions without the right to expand, and where multiplicity of options is taken for indecision.

chapters.title: 3.3. Andra — the Field of Interconnection and Time
chapters.html:
Content of the field. The third field introduces the experience of time for the first time. Its content is the process of joining and disjoining, taken as an action. Here too are located the processes of the body and the possibility of ordering them.

Phenomenology. Phenomenologically, time in this field is given as attraction: a future state acts upon the present and draws it toward itself. The metaphor of a grown tree is apt — one that, as it were, pre-exists and draws the seed toward itself; thus one configuration of reality involves another. The experience of being drawn toward a definite outcome — including the irreversibility of aging — is interpreted within this dynamic. The totality of past actions, conventionally recorded in the “seed,” subsequently determines which reality the subject will gravitate toward.

Energetic dynamics. Energy coils in a spiral inward, joining and drawing in; upon reverse rotation the spiral effects disjoining. The movement is soft yet insistent. Bodily, the field is correlated with the region of the abdomen and the lower back.

Positions of manifestation. In the position of potential — the need for joining and empathic receptivity; in the position of manifestation — the building of connections and relationships; in the position of transition — the establishment of genuine unity.

Resource expression. The resource manifestation is the capacity to restore contact and accord, to act through acceptance rather than pressure, to sense bodily processes and to bring to a timely close what has outlived itself.

Distortions. Passive distortion is merging with a loss of autonomy; active distortion, the pre-emptive severing of connections out of fear of closeness; a disturbance of transition, a stable cycle of drawing near and breaking off.

Conditions of decline. The field loses force in isolation, in environments with a ban on emotion, and where empathy is regarded as weakness.

chapters.title: 3.4. Zingra — the Field of Transformation
chapters.html:
Content of the field. The fourth field describes transformation and growth. Its content is development, aspiration and the capacity to give designs a realizable form.

Phenomenology. If the preceding field posits attraction toward the future, this field is transformation itself, proceeding continuously. What is laid within does not remain at rest but constantly sprouts: a set image begins to unfold and grow. It is a matter of bringing the inner outward, in which each subsequent turn raises the process to a new level.

Energetic dynamics. Energy unwinds in a spiral outward, carrying the inner into manifestation. The movement is ascending, active, comparable to a flame. Bodily, the field is correlated with the region between the navel and the solar plexus.

Positions of manifestation. In the position of potential — an inner impulse toward change; in the position of manifestation — the launching of processes and reforms; in the position of transition — an accomplished rebirth.

Resource expression. The resource manifestation is the constant search for a new level, the translation of desires into action, the capacity to infect others with aspiration and to use difficulties as an occasion for development.

Distortions. Passive distortion is stagnation while preserving the appearance of movement; active distortion, a ceaseless race of transformations without completing even one; a disturbance of transition, growth leading nowhere.

Conditions of decline. The field declines in stagnant systems, under work by rigid prescriptions, and where initiative is punishable.

chapters.title: 3.5. Luba — the Field of the Center
chapters.html:
Content of the field. The fifth field thematizes the center — the point and the core. Every configuration possesses a center, and its displacement alters the picture as a whole. With this field is associated concentrated attention, turned toward the present moment.

Phenomenology. Phenomenologically, attention here possesses a selective force: it is able to alter the course of events, to make a choice, to hasten transformation and to correct the initial code. Telling is the analogy with a growing tree which, meeting an obstacle, does not pass through it but goes around and nonetheless attains growth. In the capacity to select a direction consists the free will attributed to this field.

Energetic dynamics. Energy does not so much flow as gather into a point — a center of attraction toward which attention converges and from which it may radiate evenly. A stable metaphor is the flame of a candle. Bodily, the field is correlated with the region of the solar plexus and the heart.

Positions of manifestation. In the position of potential — an inner support and clarity of intention; in the position of manifestation — the acceptance of responsibility and the role of a focal point; in the position of transition — a state of concentrated presence.

Resource expression. The resource manifestation is the capacity to gather the attention of those around involuntarily, stability of self-appraisal, will without aggression, and the uniting of the heterogeneous around a common goal.

Distortions. Passive distortion is the loss of the center and dispersion; active distortion, egocentrism in which the focal point merely consumes; a disturbance of transition, a formal center devoid of content.

Conditions of decline. The field loses force where autonomy is suppressed, responsibility is blurred, and the manifestation of individuality is not permitted.

chapters.title: 3.6. Tuma — the Field of Movement
chapters.html:
Content of the field. The sixth field describes movement and even time — the sequence of events and the capacity to find oneself in accordance with circumstances. With it is associated the experience of flowing as such.

Phenomenology. Unlike the third field, which draws the subject into the future, this field is the experience of movement from within — as if a sprout were aware of its own displacement. Within its bounds an influence upon the perception of time is possible: slowing, changing the appraisal of a moment; at the same time it does not determine the final form of the outcome, acting in the present but not setting the result.

Energetic dynamics. Energy moves in a wavelike and rhythmic manner, threading events one onto another and stitching time into a coherent flow. The movement is neither spiral nor rectilinear but precisely wavelike. Bodily, the field is correlated with the region of the heart and chest.

Positions of manifestation. In the position of potential — a sense of rhythm and readiness; in the position of manifestation — action within the flow; in the position of transition — the leveling of time.

Resource expression. The resource manifestation is arriving at the fitting moment, trust in the course of events, the perception of life as an unbroken sequence, and fullness of presence in the present.

Distortions. Passive distortion is a freezing, a falling out of time; active distortion, a ceaseless running without living through; a disturbance of transition, time that does not become destiny.

Conditions of decline. The field declines in continuous chaos, under prolonged stasis, and where speed is valued to the detriment of meaning.

chapters.title: 3.7. Astra — the Field of Channels
chapters.html:
Content of the field. The seventh field discloses reality as connection. Its content is communication, movement between semantic regions, and the channels along which word and connection are transmitted.

Phenomenology. This field is opposed to the field of space. Whereas space simply is, this field is space already inhabited: within it boundaries, channels and paths have been laid. Where attention has formerly passed, stable traces arise — a kind of trodden path. It is a region in which something has already taken place — presence and absence at once.

Energetic dynamics. Energy pulsates rhythmically on the principle of a pump: reception and giving alternate, sustaining a constant exchange between the inner and the outer. Bodily, the field is correlated with the region of the throat.

Positions of manifestation. In the position of potential — inner scenarios and strategies; in the position of manifestation — communication and transmission; in the position of transition — laid channels of exchange.

Resource expression. The resource manifestation is the capacity to set forth the complex accessibly, to keep the rhythm of dialogue, to connect the formerly disjoined and to recognize the unspoken.

Distortions. Passive distortion is isolation and severed connections; active distortion, an informational noise that devalues the word; a disturbance of transition, connections in the absence of connecting meaning.

Conditions of decline. The field loses force in complete isolation, under conditions of censorship, and where communication is replaced by formal procedures.

chapters.title: 3.8. Bitra — the Field of Boundaries
chapters.html:
Content of the field. The eighth field describes boundary, form and envelope. It outlines the region within which attention is held and posits the form within which action is accomplished.

Phenomenology. Phenomenologically the field is the boundary of perception and, together with it, the movement of thought. The perceiver singles out from boundless space a center and a periphery: toward the center densification increases, toward the periphery rarefaction, up to indeterminately large scales. The subject's perception itself acts as such a center, yet the centers are many — the person, the lineage, the planet, ever more encompassing integrities. By an act of awareness the subject rebuilds the perceived architecture; thereby reality proves dependent on worldview, and its branches — traversable.

Energetic dynamics. Energy moves in a closed circle, forming a boundary within which what is happening is held, and preventing the leakage of attention outward. This is a movement of preservation and shaping. Bodily, the field is correlated with the region of the head.

Positions of manifestation. In the position of potential — a sense of one's own limits; in the position of manifestation — the establishment of outer boundaries and finished forms; in the position of transition — the reduction of boundaries to awareness.

Resource expression. The resource manifestation is the ability to mark boundaries without a sense of guilt, to hold concentration, to bring designs to a finished form and to create a space of protectedness.

Distortions. Passive distortion is a closedness that turns the boundary into a wall; active distortion, a blurring in which form is not held; a disturbance of transition, a boundary that limits but does not protect.

Conditions of decline. The field declines where refusal is impossible, where personal limits are not respected, and where constant incompleteness is required.

chapters.title: 3.9. Oma — the Field of Wholeness
chapters.html:
Content of the field. The ninth field thematizes wholeness — the joint description of all the fields. In it are equally present both orderedness subject to law and its absence; the remaining fields enter into it as facets of a single whole.

Phenomenology. The phenomenology of this field is determined by the correlation of the others. One field predetermines that with which the subject comes into consonance; another unfolds what is laid within; in the field of space much is simply foreordained, outside causal connection. It is essential that space contains no structure of itself: the subject abides in space but lives by structure, and therefore an architecture arises around it; with the entry of structure into space, life begins. Here too the mechanics of time is disclosed.

Energetic dynamics. Energy moves simultaneously in all directions, combining all the other types of movement — spirals, waves, rays and circles. Upon activation of the field an ascending flow passes along the spine, binding the fields into a single whole. Bodily, the field is correlated with the entire vertebral column.

Positions of manifestation. In the position of potential — a sense of connection with all that exists; in the position of manifestation — the synthesis of knowledge and healing action; in the position of transition — the restoration of wholeness.

Resource expression. The resource manifestation is systemic vision, the acceptance of opposites, a sense of participation in the whole, and the concord of thought, word and action.

Distortions. Passive distortion is dissolution with a loss of autonomy; active distortion, the illusion of attained fullness, a spiritually tinged presumption; a disturbance of transition, a wholeness in which the parts are indistinguishable.

Conditions of decline. The field loses force in a narrow specialization that denies connection with the whole, and in environments that reject the dimension of meaning.

chapters.title: 4. The Vertical Organization of the Fields
chapters.html:
The fields form not only a linear sequence but also a vertical structure. The upper fields — center, movement, channels and boundary — describe experience from the side of the object; the lower fields describe the inner arrangement and the path from potential to form. The relations of opposition deserve particular attention: the field of channels is correlated with the field of space as inhabited space with space as such. The first simply is; the second bears within it paths already laid and traces of former presence.

Within the upper tier the field of the center answers for selective influence in the present; the field of movement, for the experience and appraisal of the course of time without determining its outcome; the field of channels, for the manifold of shaped paths; the field of the boundary, for the reconstruction of the very architecture of perception. Jointly they set the angle at which the subject relates to the perceived object.

chapters.title: 5. The Mechanics of Time
chapters.html:
The question of the possibility of experience outside time receives a definite answer within the model. Content given as a code may be preserved in a folded, “frozen” state up until the moment when time unfolds it. Time in this sense is not a constantly operating factor: it switches on upon request, and external conditions set its course. In the state of pause time is as if absent, while remaining potentially present.

The model of the tree and the seed illustrates this proposition: a future state draws the initial one toward itself, yet upon the removal of temporal dynamics the process freezes in wait for a fitting moment. Hence follows an applied significance: work with perception becomes conceivable in which separate regions of it are held at rest while others retain mobility.

chapters.title: 6. Applied Aspect: Bodily Encoding
chapters.html:
The practical handling of the fields presupposes their bodily designation through the position of the fingers. The left hand is correlated with the position of potential, the right with the position of manifestation. In the lower tier the fields from the first to the fourth are counted from the little finger to the index finger, the same on both hands. A special role is played by the thumb, which performs the function of a switch. With the thumb held aside, the four fingers encode the fields of the lower tier; on bringing the thumb to the center of the palm the same four fingers pass to the upper tier (fields from the fifth to the eighth), and the count from the little finger takes the values from eight to five. The change of thumb position acts like a change of register on a musical instrument: with unchanged fingering a different register yields a different sound — in this case a different configuration of the fields engaged.

The work is conducted at the level of the solar plexus; essential is the experience of the passage of energy through the fingers and its turning outward. The thumb is meanwhile pressed firmly to the center of the palm. The encoding given is operational in character and serves to consolidate the described system in practice.

chapters.title: 7. Conclusion
chapters.html:
The model set forth presents perception as a system of nine stable modes, each of which possesses its own phenomenology, a characteristic energetic dynamics and three positions of manifestation. The sequence of the fields reproduces the transition from structure to wholeness, and their vertical organization demarcates the inner arrangement of experience from its objective side. The mechanics of time and the applied encoding are outlined separately.

The proposed systematization does not claim to be an exhaustive explanation and retains a descriptive status. Its value consists in the coherence of the conceptual apparatus, which allows heterogeneous states of perception and the transitions between them to be described uniformly. Further development of the model presupposes a refinement of the relations among the fields and the operationalization of the described states.

For more detailed information and practical accompaniment it is advisable to turn to the practicing masters of the DARs.
